title: Irini Starter Comp
overview: A forgiving first-clear board: Irini stacks attack speed, Nyx refreshes Rush, Reyna holds the front while you learn shop timing.
goal: Pick this when you want a simple tempo board for early Demo clears — one scaling carry, one Rush partner, one durable Warrior.
playstyle: Irini is the clock. Protect her long enough for attack-speed stacking to matter; use Nyx to keep Rush windows alive and Reyna to stop the board collapsing on contact.
positioning: Reyna front-center. Irini mid/back where she can auto safely. Nyx beside or slightly ahead of Irini so Rush partners share windows without eating the opening dive alone.
gameplan: Open: lock Irini + any real frontliner (Reyna preferred). Do not greed a third Duelist before the front holds.
First spike: Rank B Irini on the path that leans into attack speed / Stall payoffs, then Rank B Nyx if Rush uptime is the bottleneck.
Shops: take Duelist or Rush relics that fire every fight. Skip off-theme Epics you cannot trigger.
Finish: dump leftover Shards into Irini items (attack speed / Rush duration) before the challenge fight.
tips: If Irini dies first, the build is a positioning problem — not a missing legendary.
Karsu flexes in when you need Frost application; Logan flexes when you need a harder Warrior wall.
Economy relics still beat combat banners until your Rush chain actually happens every fight.
strength: Easy to understand: one carry, one enabler, one tank
Scales from common Rush / attack-speed pieces
Flex slots stay useful even if the perfect third hero never shows
weakness: Irini needs fights to stack — early burst can end her before payoff
Falls behind if you never find Rush partners or Duelist tags
Low team heal; long attrition fights need item answers

title: Rush Duelists
overview: Rip converts Rush into Max HP pressure while Nyx and Irini turn every Rush window into attack-speed snowball.
goal: Commit when you already have Rip (or another Rush-friendly Vanguard) plus at least one Duelist, and the shop keeps offering Rush duration / Endurance banners.
playstyle: You win by chaining Rush triggers, not by one giant nuke. Rip soaks and scales; Irini / Nyx print speed during those windows. If Rush rarely fires, pivot off this engine.
positioning: Rip front. Nyx secondary front or pocket so she can refresh without dying first. Irini backline. Leave a gap if enemies splash the clump.
gameplan: Stabilize Rip early — a dead Vanguard means no Rush HP engine.
Add Nyx or Irini second; the third slot can wait for Karsu (Frost) or Ming (Burn aura) if the seed leans that way.
Prioritize Rush duration and Vanguard/Duelist banners over random damage relics.
Before bosses: make sure at least two heroes benefit from the same Rush window.
tips: Count Rush triggers in a fight. If you see zero or one, fix relics / specs before buying more damage.
Ming is the flex when you want Burn + Rush Vanguard pressure instead of a third Duelist.
Do not fill the board with four Duelists and no wall — Rush comps still need someone to stand up.
strength: Multiple scaling axes (HP on Rip, speed on Duelists)
Strong mid-run once Rush is online every combat
Clear keyword identity — easy to evaluate shop offers
weakness: Collapses if Rush is interrupted or never offered
Setup-heavy: needs the right banners before it feels strong
Vulnerable to early dive on Irini / Nyx

title: Warrior Shield Core
overview: Reyna and Logan build a Warrior front that lives through contact; Kai turns shields and survival into finishing damage.
goal: Take this when Warrior banners / shield items keep appearing, or when fights last long enough for permanent growth and shield conversion to matter.
playstyle: Play for survival first. Win the opening exchange with shields and Defense, then let Logan / Kai convert leftover durability into damage. Do not greed glass cannons into the front three slots.
positioning: Logan or Reyna on the dive hex. Kai can sit secondary front or pocket if he needs to live into mid-fight. Keep any flex Mage/Mystic off the first hit.
gameplan: Early: two Warriors before fancy carries. Rowan’s Tank/Vanguard flex is fine if Reyna is missing.
Rank B the Warrior who is already winning trades — usually Logan for growth or Reyna for tempo shields.
Shop filter: Warrior + Shield text first. Crit pieces are secondary once the wall holds.
Late: one big item on the finisher (Kai / Logan), not three mediocre spreads.
tips: If you never apply shields, Shattering Charm and Amulet of Shields are dead weight — fix applicators first.
Skorn flexes when you need retaliation Tank instead of a third Warrior.
This board is slow: buy economy help so you can afford Rank spikes before challenge nodes.
strength: Shield / Warrior shops are easy to evaluate
Scales well into long fights and challenge modes
weakness: Slow clear speed without a dedicated damage spike
Feels weak if shield relics never show
Can brick if you draft three walls and no finisher

title: Mystic Sustain Field
overview: Fiona and Pollen layer shields / sustain; Grace is the panic button that recovers lost fights after Stall or wipe threats.
goal: Choose when you keep seeing Mana Regen, Shield, or Mystic banners — or when enemy packs punish short fights and you need attrition tools.
playstyle: You are not racing for first blood. Cast often, shield the lowest HP hero, and win after the enemy spike fails. Mana Regen is both uptime and coverage — starve it and the whole plan dies.
positioning: All three prefer back or second row. Put the tankiest flex (or a borrowed frontliner) ahead of them. Never leave Grace alone on a dive tile.
gameplan: Secure Fiona or Pollen early for cast loops; Grace can be the third if you are dying to burst / wipes.
Rank B toward economy (Fiona paths) or team shields — pick the path that fixes your current losses.
Items: Mana Regen and cast payoffs before raw Magic stacks.
Add one real frontliner via flex (Niklas / Gustav pocket tanks) once the support engine works.
tips: This is a support core, not a full clear squad — borrow damage from items, events, or a fourth recruit.
If casts are rare, fix Mana Regen / Max Mana before buying more shield amulets.
Sal flexes when Frost control helps; Gustav when you want a shield-zone Mystic instead of Grace.
strength: Excellent at stabilizing messy mid-run boards
weakness: Low native burst — bosses can race you
Needs frontline help from flex picks or items
Punished hard if Mystics get opened on

title: Assassin Backline
overview: Hoyoung and Yuuna delete priority targets; Zuri bridges frontline durability with Crit-scaling hybrid pressure.
goal: Force this when Crit / Assassin relics appear early and you can keep at least one diver or front piece alive long enough for backline casts and autos to land.
playstyle: Win the opening pick-off. Focus fire the threat that would kill your backline, then clean up. If Zuri (or a flex tank) falls instantly, the Assassins never get their window — fix the wall before buying more Crit.
positioning: Zuri or flex tank on first contact. Hoyoung max range back. Yuuna slightly offset so splash does not delete both carries. Use Stealth / Rush items to create a second engage angle.
gameplan: Draft one Assassin carry + one body. Do not start three squishies.
Rank B the Assassin who is already getting kills; Yuuna likes low-HP finishers, Hoyoung likes safe range.
Shop: Crit and Assassin tags first. Poison is optional payoff, not the identity.
Boss prep: one defensive item on Zuri / flex tank, damage stacked on a single carry.
tips: Dragomir flexes for execute / economy Assassin lines; Reyna / Skorn flex when you need a real wall.
Missing HP Crit items only work if someone is actually chunked — do not expect them to carry even fights alone.
If you lose because carries die first, this is not a DPS problem.
strength: Strong when Crit shops are generous
Zuri gives a hybrid front so you are not pure glass
weakness: Needs a living frontline every fight
Inconsistent if Crit never comes online
